fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is short-range ordering in bulk stainless steel rather than atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating followed by a 550 °C, 2 h anneal.

The experiment does not directly establish or quantify short-range ordering, so any corrosion difference remains confounded by grain size, phase balance, residual stress, segregation, and inclusions caused by heat treatment.
The cited evidence concerns an as-cast AlAgCuNiSnTi compositionally complex alloy in NaCl and provides no evidence that chromium short-range ordering controls passivation in stainless steel.
The principal target environments—3.5 wt% H2SO4 and 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot corrosion—are not reconstructed.
explanation: The response addresses corrosion resistance and proposes matched controls, polarization, EIS, microscopy, and a nominal falsification rule. It also overlaps generally with the target in predicting improved passivation through a chromium-rich oxide. However, it misses the defining material system, coating process, annealing series, microstructural optimum, and molten-salt conditions. Its governing cause—heat-treatment-induced short-range ordering—is neither supported by the cited paper nor directly measured in the proposed study. Because the heat treatment is unspecified and no atomically sensitive ordering measurement or mediation test is included, improved corrosion performance could not be attributed specifically to short-range ordering. The hypothesis is a potentially testable alternative in principle, but as presented it is evidentially unsupported and poorly discriminates its mechanism from ordinary heat-treatment effects.
